  <!-- annotations and the dependency block -->
  <div style="padding:0 20px 26px">
   <div class="split">
    <div class="col">
     <div class="anno"><span class="eyebrow">WHY ONE PANEL AND NOT THREE SCREENS</span>
      Brand ruled one live, non-dismissible panel on the landing screen, no modal and no time-of-day greeting. <b>The same panel is the morning reading and the closing reading.</b>
      <br><br>A modal is dismissed once and then dismissed reflexively every morning after. A separate end-of-day screen is opened on the first Friday and never again. <b>A panel that is simply there, and says something different at 18:40 than it said at 09:02, is read because it is in the way of the work.</b>
      <br><br>Press the three times in the top bar. That control is a prototype device so you can see all three readings at once. In the product there is one panel and it changes underneath the person.</div>
    </div>
    <div class="col">
     <div class="box"><h3>Voice, against Brand §4.5</h3>
      <table class="t">
       <tr><th>Not written</th><th>Written</th></tr>
       <tr><td>Good morning Ravi</td><td>Nothing. No greeting</td></tr>
       <tr><td>You were slow on 4 leads</td><td>4 leads waited over two hours for a first call</td></tr>
       <tr><td>You are 3rd of 9 on the floor</td><td>Nothing. Never a named-colleague rank on his own screen</td></tr>
       <tr><td>Great work today</td><td>1 test drive booked. 2 promises kept, 1 not</td></tr>
       <tr><td>18 points</td><td>18 points, and what each came from</td></tr>
      </table>
      <div class="xs mut" style="margin-top:9px"><b>Two tests on every line.</b> Does it carry its evidence, and is the subject the work rather than the person. The floor-rank line that was on this screen in the earlier prototype fails the second test and has been removed.</div>
     </div>
    </div>
   </div>

   <div class="box" style="margin-top:14px;border-left:3px solid var(--brass)">
    <div class="rule" style="margin-bottom:9px"></div>
    <h3>What this screen needs recorded</h3>
    <table class="t">
     <tr><th>What</th><th>Where it lives</th><th>Status</th></tr>
     <tr><td>Lead assignment, with time</td><td>Lead ledger, Phase 4</td><td><span class="pill p-ok">Schema</span></td></tr>
     <tr><td>Call attempted and connected, with duration</td><td>Lead ledger, Phase 4</td><td><span class="pill p-ok">Schema</span></td></tr>
     <tr><td>Commitments made and met</td><td><code>LEAD_EVENT_TYPES.COMMITMENT</code></td><td><span class="pill p-ok">Built</span></td></tr>
     <tr><td>Enquiry arrival time, including after hours</td><td>Lead ledger, Phase 4</td><td><span class="pill p-ok">Schema</span></td></tr>
     <tr><td>Source and campaign</td><td>Lead ledger, Phase 4</td><td><span class="pill p-ok">Schema</span></td></tr>
     <tr><td><b>Branch working hours and shifts</b></td><td>nowhere</td><td><span class="pill p-over">Not recorded</span></td></tr>
     <tr><td><b>First-response target per source</b></td><td>nowhere</td><td><span class="pill p-over">Not recorded</span></td></tr>
     <tr><td><b>Points, and what each point came from</b></td><td>Part 11, unbuilt</td><td><span class="pill p-over">Not recorded</span></td></tr>
     <tr><td><b>Lead difficulty band</b></td><td>Part 11, unbuilt</td><td><span class="pill p-over">Not recorded</span></td></tr>
    </table>
    <div class="warn" style="margin-top:12px"><b>Four lines say not recorded, and this was the safe screen.</b> Telecalling is the only fully built workspace and its day panel still needs working hours, a response target, and the points engine before it can be honest.
    <br><br><b>The one that is not optional is working hours.</b> Without it the panel tells a telecaller he was slow on a lead that arrived at 20:14, which is the single fastest way to make him stop trusting the screen. Everything else on this page can be built first and this cannot.</div>
   </div>
  </div>
 </div>
</div>
<!-- ============ DELIVERY CHAIN  SPECIFICATION ============ -->
<div class="view hidden" id="v-delivspec">
 <div class="topbar"><h1>Delivery chain</h1>
  <div class="sub">Specification for Phase 5. The operational screen is separate.</div>
  <div class="spacer"></div><span class="pill p-attn">Being built now</span></div>
 <div class="scroll" style="padding:18px 22px;background:var(--n05)">

  <div class="anno" style="margin-bottom:16px"><span class="eyebrow">WHY THIS DOCUMENT EXISTS</span>
   The product currently stops at the booking. <b><code>Booking</code> carries no promised delivery date at all</b>, and there is no promise history anywhere. So the delivery screen in this prototype is a picture of something that cannot be built from what exists.
   <br><br>This is the same screen restated as a specification, because the delivery chain is what Phase 5 is building first. <b>Everything below is either a rule the dev team can code from or a line saying nothing records it yet.</b></div>

  <!-- ============ 1. THE PROMISE ============ -->
  <div class="box" style="border-left:3px solid var(--over)">
   <div class="rule" style="margin-bottom:10px"></div>
   <h3>1. The promised date is an event, never a field</h3>
   <p class="sm mut" style="margin:0 0 12px">This is the one decision that cannot be revisited later. If the promised delivery date ships as a mutable column on <code>Booking</code>, three things become permanently unbuildable and no amount of work afterwards recovers them.</p>
   <table class="t">
    <tr><th>What breaks</th><th>Why</th></tr>
    <tr><td>The Cockpit's promise-moved-twice card</td><td>You cannot count movements of a value that only holds its current state</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Delivery promise accuracy by branch</td><td>Promised against actual needs the promise as it stood at booking, not as it stands now</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Who told the customer the 12th</td><td>The single most asked question in a delivery dispute. A field cannot answer it</td></tr>
   </table>
   <div class="warn" style="margin-top:12px"><b>Required shape.</b> A <code>DeliveryPromise</code> row per promise, append-only, carrying: the date promised, who set it, whether the person set it or the critical path computed it, and the reason if a person overrode the computation. <b>The current promise is the latest row.</b> Same pattern as <code>ExceptionEvent</code>, <code>PointEntry</code> and the lead ledger, so no new concept.</div>
   <div class="note" style="margin-top:10px"><b>And the computed date is the default, not the entry.</b> A salesperson may override it, and the override is recorded with a reason. What must never exist is a date typed with nothing behind it, which is what every dealership has today.</div>
  </div>

  <!-- ============ 2. THE STEP MASTER ============ -->
  <div class="box">
   <h3>2. The step master, and it is configuration</h3>
   <p class="sm mut" style="margin:0 0 12px">Three lanes running in parallel. The delivery date is the longest path, recomputed whenever any step changes state.</p>
   <table class="t">
    <tr><th>Lane</th><th>Step</th><th>Owner, as a Position</th><th>SLA</th><th>Blocked by</th></tr>
    <tr><td rowspan="4">Finance &amp; insurance</td><td>File submitted</td><td>F&amp;I executive</td><td>1 day from booking</td><td>Customer documents</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Sanction received</td><td>F&amp;I executive</td><td>5 days, per financier average</td><td>Financier</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Disbursement</td><td>F&amp;I executive</td><td>3 days from sanction</td><td>Financier</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Policy issued</td><td>F&amp;I executive</td><td>2 days</td><td>Disbursement</td></tr>
    <tr><td rowspan="4">Vehicle &amp; registration</td><td>Allocated</td><td>Sales admin</td><td>3 days from booking</td><td>Manufacturer</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Dispatched</td><td>Sales admin</td><td>Per manufacturer</td><td>Manufacturer</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Received at yard</td><td>Sales admin</td><td>2 days from dispatch</td><td>Transport</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Registration and plate</td><td>RTO clerk</td><td>7 days</td><td>Invoice, RTO office</td></tr>
    <tr><td rowspan="4">Preparation</td><td>Accessories ordered</td><td>Accessories</td><td>1 day from booking</td><td>Stock</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Fitment complete</td><td>Accessories</td><td>2 days from receipt</td><td>Bay capacity</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Pre-delivery check</td><td>PDI supervisor</td><td>1 day</td><td>Registration, fitment</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Handover</td><td>Sales consultant</td><td>Customer's slot</td><td>All lanes complete</td></tr>
   </table>
   <div class="note" style="margin-top:12px"><b>Owner is a Position, never a user.</b> When the RTO clerk resigns, the chain does not break and nothing needs reassigning. This is the same rule as escalation targeting the holder of a permission rather than a person.</div>
   <div class="note" style="margin-top:9px"><b>The SLA on sanction and disbursement is the financier's real average, not their claim.</b> The F&amp;I screen already measures it: SBI 3.1 days, Kotak 4.4, HDFC 6.8. A promise computed from a bank's marketing number is a promise the dealership will break.</div>
  </div>

  <!-- ============ 3. SEGMENT VARIANTS ============ -->
  <div class="box">
   <h3>3. Segments differ, and it must be seed data</h3>
   <table class="t">
    <tr><th>Segment</th><th>Steps added</th><th>Steps removed</th></tr>
    <tr><td>Petrol or diesel car</td><td>The twelve above</td><td> </td></tr>
    <tr><td>Electric vehicle</td><td>Subsidy application, charger installation survey</td><td> </td></tr>
    <tr><td>Commercial vehicle</td><td>Body building, fitness certificate, permit</td><td> </td></tr>
    <tr><td>Two-wheeler</td><td> </td><td>Allocation, often ex-stock</td></tr>
   </table>
   <div class="warn" style="margin-top:11px"><b>If adding the commercial vehicle steps needs a code change, the third brand will not be onboarded.</b> Steps, owners, SLAs and dependencies are all rows. The engine walks whatever it is given.</div>
  </div>

  <!-- ============ 4. BLOCKING ============ -->
  <div class="box">
   <h3>4. Internal and external blocks are different things</h3>
   <p class="sm mut" style="margin:0 0 12px">The distinction decides who is accountable, what the customer is told, and whether the delay affects a branch's promise accuracy.</p>
   <table class="t">
    <tr><th></th><th>Internal</th><th>External</th></tr>
    <tr><td>Example</td><td>Invoice not raised. Fitment bay full. Documents not collected</td><td>RTO office on strike. Financier slow. Manufacturer allocation</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Counts against</td><td>The step owner and the branch</td><td>Nobody. Recorded, not blamed</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Promise accuracy</td><td>Affected</td><td><b>Excluded, and the exclusion is reported</b></td></tr>
    <tr><td>Customer is told</td><td>A new date, and that we are handling it</td><td>A new date, and the honest reason</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Escalates to</td><td>The department head, then the branch head</td><td>Whoever owns the external relationship</td></tr>
   </table>
   <div class="note" style="margin-top:11px"><b>External blocks must be excluded from promise accuracy or the metric is useless.</b> A branch measured on delays caused by an RTO strike will stop trusting the number, and then stop trusting every other number on the screen. <b>But the exclusion is itself reported.</b> A branch marking everything external is visible.</div>
  </div>

  <!-- ============ 5. WHAT THE CUSTOMER SEES ============ -->
  <div class="box">
   <h3>5. The customer-facing tracker, and what it must never leak</h3>
   <div class="split">
    <div class="col">
     <table class="t">
      <tr><th>Internal step</th><th>What the customer reads</th></tr>
      <tr><td>Sanction received</td><td>Your loan is approved</td></tr>
      <tr><td>Disbursement pending, financier</td><td>Waiting for the bank to release the payment. We are chasing it daily</td></tr>
      <tr><td>Registration and plate</td><td>At the RTO for registration</td></tr>
      <tr><td>Fitment blocked, bay capacity</td><td>Accessories being fitted</td></tr>
      <tr><td>PDI</td><td>Final checks</td></tr>
     </table>
    </div>
    <div class="col">
     <div class="anno"><span class="eyebrow">THREE RULES ON THIS PAGE</span>
      <b>Never an internal step name.</b> "Waiting for the bank" not "F&amp;I lane node 3 SLA breach".
      <br><br><b>Never an internal blocker.</b> A customer is told the bank is slow, because that is true and he can understand it. He is never told our fitment bay is full, because that is our problem and saying it invites a question we do not want to answer.
      <br><br><b>Always a named human.</b> Every version of this page names the person responsible, or the customer telephones the switchboard and the whole point is lost.</div>
    </div>
   </div>
   <div class="note" style="margin-top:11px">Consent is captured on this link before any status is shown, and it covers delivery updates only. Service and offer messages need their own permission later. The link is signed and expires at delivery plus 30 days.</div>
  </div>

  <!-- ============ 6. THE DATA CONTRACT ============ -->
  <div class="box" style="border-left:3px solid var(--brass)">
   <div class="rule" style="margin-bottom:9px"></div>
   <h3>6. What this needs recorded</h3>
   <table class="t">
    <tr><th>What</th><th>Where it lives</th><th>Status</th></tr>
    <tr><td>Booking exists</td><td><code>Booking</code></td><td><span class="pill p-ok">Schema</span></td></tr>
    <tr><td>Booking value in paise</td><td><code>Booking.valueMinor</code></td><td><span class="pill p-ok">Schema</span></td></tr>
    <tr><td>Position tree, for step owners</td><td>Org tree, Phase 1</td><td><span class="pill p-ok">Schema</span></td></tr>
    <tr><td><b>Promised delivery date, as events</b></td><td>nowhere</td><td><span class="pill p-over">Not recorded</span></td></tr>
    <tr><td><b>Chain step master</b></td><td>nowhere</td><td><span class="pill p-over">Not recorded</span></td></tr>
    <tr><td><b>Step state and its transitions</b></td><td>nowhere</td><td><span class="pill p-over">Not recorded</span></td></tr>
    <tr><td><b>Blocking reason, internal or external</b></td><td>nowhere</td><td><span class="pill p-over">Not recorded</span></td></tr>
    <tr><td><b>Financier turnaround averages</b></td><td>nowhere</td><td><span class="pill p-over">Not recorded</span></td></tr>
    <tr><td><b>Segment step variants</b></td><td>nowhere</td><td><span class="pill p-over">Not recorded</span></td></tr>
    <tr><td><b>Branch working hours, for SLA in days</b></td><td>nowhere</td><td><span class="pill p-over">Not recorded</span></td></tr>
    <tr><td><b>Consent on the tracking link</b></td><td>nowhere</td><td><span class="pill p-over">Not recorded</span></td></tr>
   </table>
   <div class="warn" style="margin-top:12px"><b>Eight of eleven are not recorded, which is the honest reading of a workspace that does not exist yet.</b> Two of them decide whether the rest is worth building:
   <br><br><b>The promise as events.</b> Cheap now, impossible later, and three separate features die without it.
   <br><b>Working hours.</b> An SLA in days is meaningless without them, and the same gap already blocks the telecaller day panel. It is one table serving both, and it is the cheapest unblocking on the list.</div>
  </div>

  <div class="box">
   <h3>7. Build order, if it is mine to suggest</h3>
   <table class="t">
    <tr><th></th><th>What</th><th>Why first</th></tr>
    <tr><td>1</td><td>Working hours and shifts per branch</td><td>One small table. Unblocks every SLA in the product and the telecaller day panel as well</td></tr>
    <tr><td>2</td><td><code>DeliveryPromise</code> as an append-only ledger</td><td>Cheap now, impossible later. Everything else can follow it</td></tr>
    <tr><td>3</td><td>Step master as seed data, plus state transitions</td><td>The engine is small once the steps are rows</td></tr>
    <tr><td>4</td><td>The internal exception queue</td><td>The screen a delivery coordinator uses all day, and the first thing worth demonstrating</td></tr>
    <tr><td>5</td><td>The customer tracking link</td><td>Needs consent capture first. The referral engine, and worth waiting to get right</td></tr>
   </table>
   <div class="note" style="margin-top:11px">Steps 1 and 2 are the whole of the irreversible work. Everything from 3 onwards can be rebuilt if it is wrong.</div>
  </div>
 </div>
</div>
<!-- ============ ANALYTICS · SALES ============ -->
<div class="view hidden" id="v-an-sales">
 <div class="topbar"><h1>Sales analytics</h1><div class="sub">July 2026 · group · 5 rooftops</div>
  <div class="spacer"></div><button class="chip on">Month</button><button class="chip">Quarter</button><button class="chip">Year</button></div>
 <div class="scroll" style="padding:16px 20px;background:var(--n05)">
  <div class="mini" style="margin-bottom:14px">
   <div class="stat"><div class="v">1,691</div><div class="l">Enquiries</div></div>
   <div class="stat"><div class="v">51</div><div class="l">Deals closed, leads</div></div>
   <div class="stat"><div class="v">56</div><div class="l">Cars delivered</div></div>
   <div class="stat"><div class="v">3.0%</div><div class="l">Enquiry to deal closed</div></div>
   <div class="stat"><div class="v">₹9,642</div><div class="l">Cost per booking</div></div>
   <div class="stat"><div class="v" style="color:var(--over)">31 days</div><div class="l">Median enquiry to delivery</div></div>
  </div>
  <div class="box"><div class="rule" style="margin-bottom:10px"></div><h3>Where 1,691 enquiries went</h3>
   <div class="xs mut" style="margin:-4px 0 8px">Every step counts <b>leads</b>. Cars are counted separately below, because one lead can deliver several cars and a fleet order would otherwise distort every rate on this screen.</div>
   <div class="ch">
    <div class="ch-r"><span>Enquiries received</span><span class="ch-b"><i style="width:100%;background:var(--ink)"></i></span><span class="ch-v">1,691</span></div>
    <div class="ch-r"><span>Contacted</span><span class="ch-b"><i style="width:74%;background:var(--ink-2)"></i></span><span class="ch-v">1,251</span></div>
    <div class="ch-r"><span>Qualified</span><span class="ch-b"><i style="width:41%;background:var(--slate)"></i></span><span class="ch-v">693</span></div>
    <div class="ch-r"><span>Test drive taken</span><span class="ch-b"><i style="width:19%;background:var(--slate)"></i></span><span class="ch-v">321</span></div>
    <div class="ch-r"><span>Quotation issued</span><span class="ch-b"><i style="width:12%;background:var(--brass)"></i></span><span class="ch-v">203</span></div>
    <div class="ch-r"><span>Booked, leads</span><span class="ch-b"><i style="width:3.7%;background:var(--brass)"></i></span><span class="ch-v">62</span></div>
    <div class="ch-r"><span>Deals closed, leads</span><span class="ch-b"><i style="width:3.0%;background:var(--set)"></i></span><span class="ch-v">51</span></div>
   </div>
   <div class="split" style="margin-top:14px">
    <div class="col"><div class="box" style="margin:0;border-left:3px solid var(--brass)">
      <h3>Deals closed against cars delivered</h3>
      <table class="t">
        <tr><th>Figure</th><th>Counts</th><th class="rt">July</th></tr>
        <tr><td>Bookings</td><td>Leads that reached a booking</td><td class="rt">62</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Deals closed</td><td>Leads with at least one car delivered</td><td class="rt">51</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Cars delivered</td><td>Vehicles handed over</td><td class="rt">56</td></tr>
        <tr><td style="font-weight:700">The delivery pipeline</td><td>Booked, no car delivered yet</td><td class="rt" style="font-weight:700;color:var(--over)">11</td></tr>
      </table>
      <div class="note" style="margin-top:11px"><b>Cars exceed deals because one lead can deliver several vehicles.</b> A twelve-vehicle fleet order is one deal closed and twelve cars delivered. Any screen that treats the two as the same number will report a fleet month as a retail collapse.</div>
    </div></div>
    <div class="col"><div class="anno" style="margin:0"><span class="eyebrow">THE ELEVEN ARE THE POINT</span>
      Eleven customers have paid a booking amount and have no car. <b>That is money already committed and a promise already made</b>, and no dealer principal has ever been shown it as a single figure.
      <br><br>It is not a conversion problem and it does not belong in the funnel. It is the delivery chain, and it is the one number that says how much of last month's selling is still owed to somebody.</div></div>
  </div>
  <div class="note" style="margin-top:12px"><b>440 enquiries were never contacted at all.</b> That is the largest single drop in the funnel and it is not a market condition. At an average margin per model it represents roughly ₹39 lakh of business that never had a conversation.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="split">
   <div class="col"><div class="box"><h3>By model</h3>
    <table class="t"><tr><th>Model</th><th class="rt">Enquiries</th><th class="rt">Cars delivered</th><th class="rt">Deal rate</th><th class="rt">Cost/booking</th></tr>
    <tr><td>Grand Vitara</td><td class="rt">318</td><td class="rt">14</td><td class="rt">4.4%</td><td class="rt">₹9,200</td></tr>

   <div class="col"><div class="anno"><span class="eyebrow">WHY A VAULT AND NOT A FOLDER</span>
    A customer telephones eighteen months after delivery asking for his invoice or his insurance copy, and today somebody searches a shared drive for twenty minutes. Every document here is attached to the vehicle rather than to a deal, so it survives the salesperson leaving and the customer changing his phone.
    <br><br><b>And the missing row is the point.</b> A vault that only shows what is present is a filing cabinet. One that shows what should be present and is not is a working tool.</div></div>
   <div class="col"><div class="box"><h3>Retention and access</h3>
    <table class="t"><tr><th>Document</th><th>Held for</th><th>Who can open it</th></tr>

    <tr><td>Identity documents</td><td>Purpose only, then purged</td><td>F&amp;I only, logged on every open</td></tr></table>
    <div class="note" style="margin-top:10px">Identity documents are the sensitive category. They are held for the finance application and purged when it closes, and every single view is written to the audit log with a name against it.</div>

   <div class="anno"><span class="eyebrow">SAME ENGINE, DIFFERENT OUTCOMES</span>
    This seat uses the telecalling console, the recording, the points and the anti-gaming rules unchanged. <b>Only the outcome set differs</b>: booked, rescheduled, declined with a reason, wants pick-up, already serviced elsewhere.
    <br><br>That last one matters. A customer who says he serviced at a local garage is a win-back with a reason, and the reason is worth counting.</div>
   <div class="eyebrow" style="margin:18px 0 8px">SERVICE DUE IS PREDICTED</div>
   <div class="sm mut">Not a six-month reminder to everybody. Due date comes from this vehicle's own usage, roughly 8,900 km a year for the first row, so the call lands when the car actually needs work.</div>

   </div>
  </div>
  <div class="anno"><span class="eyebrow">WHY THIS IS WORTH BUILDING</span>
   Manufacturer reporting is the least glamorous feature in this product and one of the most persuasive. <b>A dealer's team currently spends five to eight hours a month assembling these by hand from three systems, and the figures never quite agree.</b>
   <br><br>Because every number in Arth is defined once in the metrics engine, the manufacturer report and the dealer principal's screen cannot disagree. That is not a reporting feature, it is the reason a general manager will argue for keeping the product.</div>
 </div>
</div>

    A target is an outcome and largely outside one person's control. Points are behaviour and entirely within it.
    <br><br><b>Missing a target never removes a point.</b> A poor month in a slow market must not teach a good executive that behaving well is worthless, because the next thing he does is stop recording leads honestly.</div>

   <div class="col"><div class="anno"><span class="eyebrow">WHY THIS SCREEN ENDS ARGUMENTS</span>
    Incentive disputes are the most common source of friction on a dealership floor, and they happen because the calculation lives in somebody's spreadsheet.
    <br><br><b>Every line here traces to a delivered car, a recorded call or an issued policy.</b> An executive who disagrees can open the trace himself. That is worth more than the accuracy, because the accuracy was never really the problem.</div></div>
   <div class="col"><div class="box"><h3>Arth stops at the number</h3>
    <p class="sm mut" style="margin:0">It computes what is payable and exports it. <b>It never pays anybody, never touches a bank account and never holds a salary.</b> Payroll is a regulated system with statutory filings, and building one would be the largest scope error available to this product.</p>
   </div></div>

   <div class="col"><div class="anno"><span class="eyebrow">STEP 3 IS THE ONE THAT BLOCKS EVERYTHING</span>
    Working hours look like the dullest step on this list and they gate every clock in the product. Without them the system penalises a telecaller for a lead that arrived at 21:40, and the floor stops trusting the screen in its first week.
    <br><br><b>Nothing else should go live until step 3 is complete for every branch.</b></div></div>
   <div class="col"><div class="box"><h3>Migration, and the honest version of it</h3>
    <p class="sm mut" style="margin:0 0 10px">A dealer's existing customer data will contain the same person three times with three spellings and two numbers. <b>Arth shows you the duplicates and you decide</b>, because an automatic merge that joins two households is a mistake nobody can unpick later.</p>
    <p class="sm mut" style="margin:0">Expect this to take a week and expect it to be tedious. Every vendor who promises a one-click import is either not migrating much or is about to corrupt a database.</p>
   </div></div>

function openIdx(){
 var el=document.getElementById('idxBody');
 if(!el.innerHTML){
  var h='';
  INDEX.forEach(function(g){
   h+='<div class="idx-g"><h4>'+g[0]+'</h4><div class="d">'+g[1]+'</div><div class="idx-l">';
   g[2].forEach(function(s){
    h+='<div class="idx-i" onclick="fromIdx(\''+s[0]+'\')"><b>'+s[1]+'</b><span>'+s[2]+'</span></div>';
   });
   h+='</div></div>';
  });
  el.innerHTML=h;
 }
 document.getElementById('idx').classList.add('on');
}
function closeIdx(){document.getElementById('idx').classList.remove('on')}
function fromIdx(v){
 closeIdx();
 var has=false;
 ROLES[ROLE].groups.forEach(function(g){g[1].forEach(function(i){if(i[0]===v)has=true})});
 if(!has){
  var found=null;
  Object.keys(ROLES).forEach(function(k){
   if(found) return;
   ROLES[k].groups.forEach(function(g){g[1].forEach(function(i){if(i[0]===v&&!found)found=k})});
  });
  if(found&&found!==ROLE){
   ROLE=found; curView=v; buildNav(); showView(v);
   document.querySelectorAll('.nav-i').forEach(function(n){n.classList.toggle('on',n.dataset.go===v)});
   toast('Viewing as '+ROLES[found].who+', '+ROLES[found].name);
   return;
  }
 }
 go(v);
}

var ROLE='tele', curView='tele';

function buildNav(){
 var r=ROLES[ROLE], h='';
 r.groups.forEach(function(g){
  h+='<div class="nav-h">'+g[0]+'</div>';
  g[1].forEach(function(i){
   h+='<a class="nav-i'+(i[0]===curView?' on':'')+'" data-go="'+i[0]+'" tabindex="0">'
    +'<svg class="ic"><use href="#'+i[1]+'"/></svg><span>'+i[2]+'</span>'
    +(i[3]?'<span class="c'+(i[4]?' bad':'')+'">'+i[3]+'</span>':'')+'</a>';
  });
 });
 h+='<div class="nav-h">ALL SCREENS</div><a class="nav-i" onclick="openIdx()" tabindex="0"><svg class="ic"><use href="#i-scale"/></svg><span>Platform index</span></a>';
 h+='<div class="notes-t" id="notesT" onclick="toggleNotes()"><span class="lbl">Build notes<br><span style="color:var(--on-ink-dim)">for you and the IT team</span></span><span class="sw"><i></i></span></div>';
 document.getElementById('navBody').innerHTML=h;
 applyRoleClass();
 document.getElementById('roleName').textContent=r.name;
 document.getElementById('whoName').textContent=r.who;
 document.getElementById('whoRole').textContent=r.sub;
 bindNav();
}
function bindNav(){
 document.querySelectorAll('.nav-i').forEach(function(n){
  if(!n.dataset.go) return;
  n.onclick=function(){ go(n.dataset.go) };
  n.onkeydown=function(e){ if(e.key==='Enter'||e.key===' '){e.preventDefault();go(n.dataset.go)} };
 });
}
function toggleRoles(){
 var m=document.getElementById('roleMenu');
 if(!m.innerHTML){
  var h='';
  Object.keys(ROLES).forEach(function(k){
   h+='<a onclick="setRole(\''+k+'\')" class="'+(k===ROLE?'on':'')+'">'+ROLES[k].name
    +'<small>'+ROLES[k].who+'</small></a>';
  });
  m.innerHTML=h;
 }
 m.classList.toggle('hidden');
}
function setRole(k){
 ROLE=k; document.getElementById('roleMenu').classList.add('hidden');
 document.getElementById('roleMenu').innerHTML='';
 var first=ROLES[k].groups[0][1][0][0];
 curView=first; buildNav(); showView(first);
 toast('Now signed in as '+ROLES[k].who+', '+ROLES[k].name+'. The menu changes with the role.');
}

function showView(v){
 document.querySelectorAll('.view').forEach(function(e){e.classList.add('hidden')});
 var t=document.getElementById('v-'+v); if(t) t.classList.remove('hidden');
 var sc=document.querySelector('#v-'+v+'.scroll'); if(sc) sc.scrollTop=0;
}
function applyRoleClass(){
 var sees=(ROLE==='mgr'||ROLE==='owner'||ROLE==='adv'||ROLE==='lead'||ROLE==='admin');
 document.body.classList.toggle('exec',!sees);
}
function go(v){
 var d=document.getElementById('dirtybar'); if(d) d.classList.remove('on');
 applyRoleClass();
 curView=v; showView(v); animateView(v);
 document.querySelectorAll('.nav-i').forEach(function(n){
  n.classList.toggle('on', n.dataset.go===v);
 });
}

/* ---------- unsaved changes ---------- */
function markSaved(id){
 var el=document.getElementById(id);
 if(el) el.textContent='Saved just now';
 document.getElementById('dirtybar').classList.remove('on');
 toast('Saved');
}
document.addEventListener('input',function(e){
 if(e.target.closest('.view') && (e.target.tagName==='INPUT'||e.target.tagName==='TEXTAREA'||e.target.tagName==='SELECT')){
  document.getElementById('dirtybar').classList.add('on');
 }
});
function discardChanges(){document.getElementById('dirtybar').classList.remove('on');toast('Changes discarded')}

/* ---------- toast ---------- */
var tEl=document.getElementById('toast'), tT;
function toast(m){ tEl.textContent=m; tEl.classList.add('show');
 clearTimeout(tT); tT=setTimeout(function(){tEl.classList.remove('show')},3400); }

/* ---------- drawer ---------- */
function openDrawer(){
 document.getElementById('drawerTitle').textContent='Audit trail';
 document.getElementById('drawerSub').textContent='Permanent record · nothing can be edited';
 document.getElementById('drawerBody').innerHTML=AUDIT;
 document.getElementById('drawer').classList.add('open');
 document.getElementById('ov').classList.add('on');
}
function closeDrawer(){document.getElementById('drawer').classList.remove('open');document.getElementById('ov').classList.remove('on')}
document.addEventListener('keydown',function(e){if(e.key==='Escape'){closeDrawer();closeIdx()}});

/* ---------- motion ---------- */
var REDUCE = window.matchMedia && window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;

function animateView(v){
 var el=document.getElementById('v-'+v); if(!el) return;
 if(REDUCE) return;

 // bars: remember the target once, then grow from zero
 el.querySelectorAll('.ch-b i, .bar-h i').forEach(function(b){
  if(!b.dataset.w) b.dataset.w=b.style.width||'0%';
  b.style.transition='none'; b.style.width='0%';
 });

 // rows and cards arrive in sequence
 var seq=el.querySelectorAll('.lrow, .stat, .qr');
 seq.forEach(function(n,i){ n.style.animationDelay=Math.min(i*26,320)+'ms'; });

 el.classList.remove('anim'); void el.offsetWidth; el.classList.add('anim');

 requestAnimationFrame(function(){
  requestAnimationFrame(function(){
   el.querySelectorAll('.ch-b i, .bar-h i').forEach(function(b){
    b.style.transition=''; b.style.width=b.dataset.w;
   });
   countUp(el);
  });
 });
}

// headline figures count up. Only .stat .v, never a figure inside a table,
// because a table of moving numbers is unreadable.
function countUp(el){
 // Figures render at their final value immediately.
 // A counting animation shows false numbers for ~2 seconds, and this screen
 // is designed to be read in ninety. Removed deliberately, not overlooked.
 el.querySelectorAll('.stat .v').forEach(function(n){
  if(n.dataset.txt) n.textContent=n.dataset.txt;
 });
}
function indianGroup(s){
 var parts=s.split('.'), n=parts[0];
 if(n.length<=3) return s;
 var last3=n.slice(-3), rest=n.slice(0,-3);
 rest=rest.replace(/\B(?=(\d{2})+(?!\d))/g,',');
 return rest+','+last3+(parts[1]?'.'+parts[1]:'');
}

/* the only looping motion in the product: a clock that is genuinely running */
var jobMins=42;
setInterval(function(){
 var v=document.getElementById('v-job');
 if(!v||v.classList.contains('hidden')||REDUCE) return;
 jobMins++;
 var n=document.getElementById('jobNow'), o=document.getElementById('jobOver');
 var t=11*60+jobMins;
 if(n) n.textContent=String(Math.floor(t/60)).padStart(2,'0')+':'+String(t%60).padStart(2,'0');
 if(o) o.textContent=jobMins+' min over promise';
},3000);

/* ---------- build notes toggle ---------- */
function tagSpec(){
 document.querySelectorAll('.anno').forEach(function(a){
  a.classList.add('spec');
  var box=a.closest('.box'); if(box && box.querySelectorAll('.anno').length && box.children.length<=2) box.classList.add('spec');
  var col=a.parentElement;
  if(col && col.classList.contains('col') && col.children.length===1) col.classList.add('spec');
 });
 document.querySelectorAll('.box h3').forEach(function(h){
  if(/^(Why |What this screen needs|Voice, against|The rule that|Build order|Two rules|Three rules)/.test(h.textContent))
   h.closest('.box').classList.add('spec');
 });
}
function toggleNotes(){
 var on=!document.body.classList.contains('notes-off');
 document.body.classList.toggle('notes-off',on);
 var t=document.getElementById('notesT');
 if(t) t.classList.toggle('notes-on',!on);
 toast(on?'Build notes hidden. This is what a dealer sees.'
     :'Build notes shown. These are for you and the IT team, never for a user.');
}

 } else if(disp==='nc'){

}
function saveDisp(){
 if(!disp){ toast('Choose what happened on the call before saving'); return; }
 var base={td:8,visit:5,quote:4,fu:1,post:1,lost:0,nc:0}[disp]||0;
 var band=LEADS[cur].band||'Warm';
 var mult={'Hot':1,'Warm':1.5,'Cold':2.5,'Very cold':3.5}[band]||1;
 var gain=Math.round(base*mult);

 pts+=gain;

 document.getElementById('ptsBar').style.width=Math.min(100,Math.round(pts/45*100))+'%';
 LEADS[cur].done=true; doneCount++;
 var msg='Saved. '+(gain?('+'+gain+' points, '+base+' × '+mult+' for a '+band.toLowerCase()+' lead')
  :'No points, correctly, this call did not produce anything');
 if(disp==='post') msg='Saved. Lead parked until 20 Aug and still open. +'+gain+' points.';

 toast(msg);
 var nxt=LEADS.findIndex(function(l){return !l.done});
 if(nxt>=0){ pickLead(nxt); } else { resetCall(); renderQueue(); toast('Queue finished. 6 calls, '+pts+' points.'); }
}

 var e=document.getElementById('lostExtra');
 if(!e) return;
 e.innerHTML = v && m[v] ? '<div class="fld"><label>'+m[v]+'</label>'
  +(v==='stop'?'<div class="warn" style="margin:0">This customer will be removed from calls, WhatsApp, SMS and from advertising audience lists within minutes.</div>'
   :'<input class="inp" placeholder="Required">')+'</div>' : '';
}
function cancelDisp(){ resetCall(); toast('Nothing recorded, the call still appears in the audit trail'); }

 });
 ['bays','bays2'].forEach(function(id){var el=document.getElementById(id); if(el) el.innerHTML=h;});
})();

(function(){

# BUILD ORDER · TELECALLING FLOOR, PASS 2

**For:** the Arth clean-room build
**Date:** 26 August 2026
**Source of truth:** this file, then `docs/books/`
**Scope:** the telecalling floor only. Seven screens. Nothing else.

---

## §0 READ THIS BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE

**This is a correction pass on a floor that already works.** Pass 1 built it and it was reviewed. Most of it was right. This file lists what to change and what to leave alone.

**Do not rebuild anything.** The foundation is correct: forced row-level security, append-only ledgers by privilege, working hours gating the clock, money in paise, nine stages as rows, undo as a correcting entry. **All of that stays exactly as it is.**

### Hard stops

**Build only these seven screens:**
`Sign in` · `Today` · `Log a call` · `My enquiries` · `Enquiry record` · `Search` · `File an enquiry` · `Notifications` · `My profile`

**Do not build, do not scaffold, do not stub:**

| Not this cycle | Why |
|---|---|
| **Any score or points screen** | Points need call duration to enforce a 20-second connect floor. Duration needs telephony. No provider is chosen. **Shipping a score before its anti-gaming control exists teaches a floor to game it** |
| **Any manager screen** | Floor today, Assignment, Team scores, Why we lose, Response times. Designed, not in scope |
| **Any dealer principal screen** | Decisions, What bookings cost, Compare branches |
| **Any Advito screen** | Admin or support |
| **Telephony of any kind** | No dialler, no recording, no duration capture |
| **Sales, service, delivery, insurance, used car** | Descoped by the client |

**If you think one of the above is needed to make something else work, stop and ask.** Do not build it and explain afterwards.

---

## §1 THE ORDER OF WORK

Five batches. **Finish and report each batch before starting the next.** Do not combine them into one commit.

| Batch | What | Why this order |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | The two defects that block a demonstration | Nothing can be shown until these are fixed |
| **2** | Seed data | Everything visible depends on it |
| **3** | Layout corrections | Safe, visible, easy to review |
| **4** | Copy corrections | Cosmetic, fast |
| **5** | Proofs | Confirms 1 to 4 actually hold |

---

## §2 BATCH 1 · THE TWO DEFECTS

### 1.1 · The disposition panel must not open with an outcome chosen

**Where:** Log a call, the disposition panel.

**Now:** `initial` is `dispositions[0].key`, so the panel opens showing `Connected, callback` with its revisit field. `Record outcome` is never disabled and validation happens only after the request is sent.

**Why this is the most serious defect on the floor:** a telecaller can press save without ever choosing an outcome, and what gets written is a connection. Forty times a morning. **Nothing errors. The ledger simply says the floor performed better than it did**, which is the exact failure the product exists to end.

**Change:**

1. The outcome select opens with **no selection**, showing `Select an outcome`.
2. **No conditional field renders until an outcome is chosen.** Revisit date must not be on screen before an outcome that requires it is picked.
3. `Record outcome` is **disabled** until an outcome is chosen and every field that outcome requires is filled. Validate on the client, not only on the server.
4. Changing the outcome after fields are filled **clears the fields that no longer apply.**

**Requirements by outcome, unchanged from pass 1:**

| Outcome | Requires |
|---|---|
| Connected, callback | Revisit date. Plus a reason if more than 14 days out |
| Postponed | Revisit date. Same 14-day rule |
| Lost | Lost reason, then the specific fact that reason demands |
| Not connected · busy / switched off / no answer | Nothing beyond an optional note |

### 1.2 · The offline banner must not promise sync

**Where:** the offline banner, all screens.

**Now:** it says calls will sync. **There is no offline write queue.**

**Change:** remove the sync claim. State that the connection is lost and work cannot be saved right now.

**Do not build an offline queue in this pass.** Fixing the sentence is the whole task.

### 1.3 · Revisit is a date, not a date and time

**Now:** `datetime-local`.

**Change:** date only. **A telecaller does not know the hour, and a fabricated hour in a ledger is worse than no hour.**

---

## §3 BATCH 2 · SEED DATA

### 2.1 · Seed events, not stages

**Now:** leads are seeded directly at a stage. The result is Meera Joshi at `Negotiation` (7 of 9) and Priya Menon at `Test drive` (5 of 9), both showing **"No activity recorded."**

**Why this cannot ship:** the product's central claim is that every enquiry carries a ledger. **The first card a reviewer sees says the ledger is empty on a lead six stages deep.** They do not know it is seed data.

**Change:** every seeded lead must be walked up the ladder by inserting `lead_events`, with its stage following from that history. **A lead's stage must be reachable from its own events.**

Each event needs a plausible actor, timestamp inside working hours, and where relevant a disposition and note.

### 2.2 · More volume

**Now:** roughly eight enquiries per telecaller.

**Change:** **30 to 40 per telecaller**, with a realistic age spread.

**Why:** a floor with eight enquiries cannot demonstrate a queue that empties, and a dealer principal judges believability by the shape of the book. It should look like a Tuesday, not a fixture file.

Keep the four named walk-through cases exactly as they are: **Ramesh Kumar, Anita Desai, Fazal Ahmed and the S. Rao refusal.**

---

## §4 BATCH 3 · LAYOUT

### 3.1 · Nine fields, not seven, at desktop

**Now:** `lg:grid-cols-[1.5fr 1fr 0.9fr 0.9fr 1.2fr 1.2fr 6.5rem]`, with name, phone, enquiry number and status stacked together in column one.

**Change:** at `lg` and above, split column one into four separate columns.

**The nine, in order:**

| | Field | Note |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Customer name | |
| 2 | Phone | Monospace |
| 3 | Enquiry number | Monospace |
| 4 | Status stamp | `OVERDUE` / `PARKED` / blank |
| 5 | Vehicle | Model over variant |
| 6 | Source | Source over location |
| 7 | Stage | Name over `n of 9` |
| 8 | **Last activity** | **The event, then the date.** "Called, no answer · 03 Aug". Never a bare date |
| 9 | Next | What is due and when. Overdue in `--arth-overdue` |

**Below `lg` the current stacked card is correct. Keep it.** Column headings render at `lg` and above only.

### 3.2 · Remaining count on the Late heading

**Add** a count on the right of the Late block heading: `6 remaining`. **It must decrease when a call is logged.**

**Why:** a queue's whole value is that it falls. A number that does not visibly decrease is a list, and a list does not feel finishable.

### 3.3 · Parked as a stamp

**Now:** plain uppercase text. **Change:** a stamp, same treatment as `OVERDUE`, using `--arth-brass-wash` on `--arth-brass-pill`.

### 3.4 · Sign in must not show floor chrome

**Now:** a signed-in visitor to `/w/login` sees the nav tiles and Log out above the sign-in form.

**Change:** either redirect a signed-in visitor to their landing, or render this route with the ink band showing the wordmark only.

### 3.5 · Notifications: one target per row

**Now:** the whole row is clickable **and** there is a separate Open button.

**Change:** remove the button. The row is the target.

---

## §5 BATCH 4 · COPY

### 4.1 · The render artifact in the enquiry number

**Now:** `Enquiry <!-- -->FFFFFFF7` in the markup. **Change:** remove the artifact. The enquiry number goes onto paperwork and into Search; a copy-paste carrying a comment is a support call nobody will diagnose quickly.

### 4.2 · Marketing page defects

| | Now | Change |
|---|---|---|
| **Headline layout** | One word per line, running off the viewport | Size the type for the container it is in |
| **"artha"** | *"One delivered car is artha."* | **The mark is `arth`.** Two spellings in one viewport is a problem a dealer notices before he notices the software |
| **The ₹9,200 line** | *"those forty calls cost ₹9,200 and produced one delivered car"* | **₹9,200 is cost per booking for one campaign. It is not the cost of forty calls.** As written it reads as ₹230 per telephone call, which is not a claim we make. Rewrite it to say what is true, or use a figure that means what the sentence says |

### 4.3 · Copy that must not change

These are correct and better than the specification. **Leave them exactly as written:**

- *"Hours are not on file for this branch. Clocks cannot be trusted until they are."*
- *"No rows yet. The first call writes the first row. Rows are never edited."*
- *"Undo writes a correcting entry. The original row stays."*
- *"This screen is for another seat."*
- *"Every one says why you got it."*

---

## §6 BATCH 5 · PROOFS

Two additions to `npm run prove`. Both must print their token.

### `db:ledger` → `LEDGER_OK`

Assert **no lead beyond the `contacted` stage has zero `lead_events`.** This is what stops 2.1 regressing.

### `db:queue` → `QUEUE_OK`

Take a seat's queue count for today. Log one disposition with a future revisit date. Assert the count **decreased by exactly one** and that the lead now derives as `Parked`.

**Every existing proof must still pass.** If one breaks, stop and report it rather than adjusting the proof.

---

## §7 DO NOT TOUCH

| Leave alone | Reason |
|---|---|
| `withTenant`, RLS policies, `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` | Correct and expensive to get wrong |
| `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE` on any ledger | Correct |
| Working hours, the clock, after-hours assignment | Correct, and proven |
| The undo mechanism | Correct. Writes a correction, restores from payload |
| Auto-advance after ~1500ms | Correct. This is the ruling working |
| The 403 refusal at the same URL | Correct. Do not change it to a redirect |
| Today's three-block split | Correct. Late first |
| The token block | 21 tokens. **Do not add a colour without asking** |
| `Log a call` as the screen name | Correct. Better than "On a call" |

---

## §8 HOW TO REPORT BACK

After each batch, write to `docs/PASS-2-STATUS.md` and stop.

**For each item in the batch:**

1. **What changed**, with the file and the line.
2. **What did not change**, and why.
3. **Anything that turned out to be already correct.** Say so; do not pretend to have fixed it.
4. **Anything you disagreed with**, and what you did instead.

**After batch 5, add:**

- The full terminal output of `npm run prove`.
- A list of the nine routes with a one-line note on what a reviewer will see at each.
- **Screenshots of `Today`, `Log a call` with the outcome unselected, `Log a call` after saving, and one enquiry record with its ledger**, at 1440px wide.

**Label every claim** `VERIFIED` if you ran it, `SPEC` if a document says so, `ASSUMED` if you are guessing.

**If anything in this file contradicts something in `docs/books/`, say so rather than choosing.** These documents have been reviewed carefully, so a contradiction is a real defect and worth knowing about.

# CONTROL SEATS — TELECALLING SET

**Ruled 27 August 2026.** This is the first control set. Other department managers
are not these seats.

## Dealer seats in this set

| Seat | Username (demo) | Role key | Lands on | Bucket |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Digital desk manager | gupta / fernandes | `mgr` | The floor `/w/desk` | This branch, telecalling team only |
| Dealer principal | shah / kamath | `owner` | This dealer `/w/prin` | This dealer only |
| Team leader | menon | `lead` | My enquiries | The team (already on the floor) |

The digital desk places a name onto a telecaller when the floor needs a direction.
Until then the shared book until reach still holds. The desk does not run sales,
service, or any other department.

The dealer principal sees telecalling health at this dealer. Not the Exception
Cockpit. Not another dealer.

Every dealer seat in this set has **Performance analysis** (`/w/perf`, and on the
landing screen). It reads the live book for that seat only: what is holding, what
is late or still shared, and what to execute next. It is not a target-entry form.
Targets still come from the superior. Advito reads dealer walls on Dealers, then
one dealer at a time for floor figures.

## Advito seats

Advito operators are **not** dealer users. They live on `platform_users`. A missing
platform session cannot read a dealer row.

| Seat | Username (demo) | Can onboard | Can enter a dealer |
|---|---|---|---|
| Advito admin | advito | Yes | One dealer at a time |
| Advito support | support | No | One dealer at a time, logged |

Support exists in this set so a client problem can be fixed without mixing dealers.
Support does not see Advito commercial terms (none are shown on this seat). Entering
a dealer uses a per-dealer `ops` shadow. Enquiry RLS is still that dealer only.

Admin onboards: dealer wall, branch hours, stages, dispositions, principal, digital
desk, one telecaller.

## What is not this set

Branch managers of other departments. Sales managers. Workshop. Exception Cockpit.
Master pricing. Engineering health. Those wait until this telecalling control set
is signed off.

# DECISION LOG

Append only. Never edit a past entry; supersede it with a new one.
Read this before designing anything.

---

## 2026-08-27 · Telecalling control seats, then other departments
Digital desk manager runs the telecalling team at a branch. Dealer principal sees this dealer only. Advito admin onboards dealers. Advito support enters one dealer at a time to fix a floor problem, logged. Support cannot onboard. No dealer sees another dealer. Other department managers wait. Law: `docs/books/CONTROL-SEATS.md`.

## 2026-08-26 · Four visibility walls, every department
Dealer, then branch, then team, then owner. After a telecaller reaches the customer, Search and Filter hide that enquiry from other telecallers. Team leader sees the team. Branch manager sees the branch. Dealer principal sees this dealer only. Forced RLS plus `arth_lead_visible`. Fail closed without `app.user_id`. Law: `docs/books/VISIBILITY-WALLS.md`. Sales, service, and every later department inherit this. A bypass is a defect.

## 2026-08-26 · Shared book until reach, then exclusive
New names are visible to every telecaller at the branch until a connected call of 20 seconds or more. Then the owner is the telecaller who reached the customer. Not-connected outcomes do not claim.

## 2026-08-26 · Telecalling qualifies, sales converts
Hand to sales is allowed from Qualified. Conversion is the sales consultant's job. Today stays a telecalling screen.

---

## 2026-08-21 · Nine stages, not twelve
`New · Assigned · Contacted · Qualified · Test drive · Quotation · Negotiation · Booked · Delivered`
Twelve folded delivery-chain steps into the sales pipeline. Allocated, Invoiced and Registered are chain steps. Modelling them twice means two places to disagree about where a car is. After Booked, progress is the chain's to report.

## 2026-08-21 · The telecaller queue is their day
Enquiries due today plus anything breaching. Not everything callable. **It decrements as calls are logged.** Everything else lives in My enquiries.

## 2026-08-21 · In-place confirmation, not a toast
At forty times a morning a toast becomes chrome. The disposition panel becomes the confirmation for ~1.5s: what was recorded, what it earned, what happens next. Undo inside that window, as a correcting entry.

## 2026-08-21 · Expected value formula
`(unit gross + attached gross) x stage probability`. Attached at its own attach rate, average case. Seeded defaults at launch, replaced by the dealer's own after month one, marked provisional until then. A ranking device before a reported figure.

## 2026-08-21 · Parked is derived
Latest disposition is POSTPONED and revisit date is future. Never stored.

## 2026-08-21 · A seat carries workspaceKey
Exactly one landing workspace, never a chooser. Landing is not permission.

## 2026-08-21 · Call duration gates the points engine
Not needed for the demo. The 20-second connect floor cannot be enforced without it. Do not ship points first.

## 2026-08-21 · Household + service line is Phase 6
Ship the weak version now from data already held. Same slot, stronger line later.

## 2026-08-18 · Green action button withdrawn
The Book gives five variants and none is green. Settled is semantic and never decorates. Ink fill measures 15.01:1 against the green's 6.83:1, so the Book's own primary also solves the contrast failure that prompted it.

## 2026-08-18 · Text on brass-wash is --arth-brass-pill #7A5716
It already existed, added in palette v2.2 for this exact pairing. brass-deep measures 4.19:1 there and fails.

## 2026-08-18 · Three metric names, never interchangeable
Bookings = leads reaching a booking. Deals closed = leads with at least one car delivered. Cars delivered = vehicles. Conversion uses the lead numerator. One lead can deliver several cars.

## 2026-08-17 · The delivery promise is an event, never a field
Every movement writes a new row. Without it: cannot count how often a promise moved, cannot measure accuracy against the original, cannot answer who told the customer the 12th.

## 2026-08-17 · Difficulty is computed at assignment and frozen
System-computed, never manager-set. Hidden from the executive. Bands x1.0 / x1.5 / x2.5 / x3.5.

## 2026-08-17 · Compare branches on process, not outcome
First response, contact rate, test drive rate, promise accuracy. A comparison on cars sold turns every review into an argument about market conditions.

## 2026-08-17 · Margin is dealer-admin only. Salary never below the principal
Not configurable. An insurance executive gets a ranked recommendation with reasons and no margin figure.

## Standing · A threshold about human behaviour is set from real behaviour
First pilot month. Never invented in advance.

## Standing · Report, never silently correct
Reconciliation reports disagreements. A silent auto-correction destroys the evidentiary value of a ledger.
```

> **Archived memo, 21 August 2026.** Retained for the reasoning. The rulings here
> are settled and reflected in `DECISIONS.md`, which is authoritative. The prototype
> copy referred to in Q2 has since been updated: it reads nine stages throughout.

# THE EIGHT DECISIONS — ANSWERED

**From:** Director, Product Engineering
**To:** Development team, Advito Global · cc IT Director · Prem Kumar
**Date:** 21 August 2026
**Re:** `ARTH-BUILD-STATE-for-product-director.html`

You asked for a paragraph each. That is what this is. Three block the demonstration and they are answered first.

**Before the eight, one correction in your favour and one thing that is Prem's.**

**Compare has a counterpart.** Your table records *"no counterpart — built this week"* for `/w/…/compare`. It is **Compare branches** in the prototype, and it carries a design position worth having before you go further: compare on **process**, not outcome. First response, contacted-in-24h, test drive rate, promise accuracy — because a comparison on cars sold turns every review into an argument about market conditions, and a comparison on response time cannot be argued with. Check it before building more of that screen.

**Prem: run the seed.** One person can sign in, eighteen accounts have no password, and the data ages a day every day. The access model is the thing that distinguishes Arth from a shared spreadsheet and it cannot currently be shown at all. The operation is built and rehearsed. It needs you.

---

## Q1 · The queue is their day. Not everything callable.

**Their day.** A count that does not move while you work is worse than no count, and 162 is not a morning — it is a filing cabinet.

**Definition: every enquiry whose next action falls on or before today, plus anything currently breaching its first-response window.** Nothing else. An enquiry with a callback set for Monday is not in Tuesday's queue and must not be counted in it.

**And it decrements.** Log a call, the number falls. That is most of the value of the figure. Everything else callable lives in *My enquiries*, which is a different screen with a different job — the queue is a morning with an end, the pipeline is the whole book.

One consequence to build in from the start: when the queue empties, it says so and offers the next-best work rather than showing zero and stopping. A telecaller at 15:00 with an empty queue is the one moment the product can hand him revival leads.

---

## Q2 · Nine stages, and the twelve was my error

I over-specified. Twelve folded the delivery chain into the sales pipeline, and that was defensible before the chain became its own object with its own steps and owners. **It is now duplication: Allocated, Invoiced and Registered are chain steps, not sales stages, and modelling them twice means two places to disagree about where a car is.**

**The nine, in order:**

`New · Assigned · Contacted · Qualified · Test drive · Quotation · Negotiation · Booked · Delivered`

**A stage answers *how far along is this*, and only for work the salesperson controls.** After Booked, progress is the delivery chain's to report, and the lead simply reads Booked until a car is handed over.

**Two things that are not stages:** *Lost* is a terminal state with a required reason. *Parked* is derived — see Q7. Neither belongs in the ladder.

Your seven is closer to right than my twelve was. The two I would add back are **Assigned**, because unassigned is a real condition a manager acts on, and **Quotation**, because a quotation issued is the strongest pre-booking signal in the funnel and currently disappears inside Negotiation.

**The prototype copy is mine to change — every row reading *3 of 12* becomes *3 of 9*.** That cost is on my side, not yours.

---

## Q3 · The panel confirms in place. Not a toast.

You are right that a prototype rarely shows the moment after, and mine does not. It uses a toast, and **a toast is wrong at this frequency** — forty times a morning it becomes chrome and stops being read, and it is dismissible, so it can be missed entirely.

**On save, the disposition panel itself becomes the confirmation, in place, for about a second and a half.** It states three things: what was recorded, what it earned, and what happens next — *"Postponed. Revisit 20 August. +3 points, cold lead."* Then the next call loads beneath it.

**The confirmation lives inside the thing that changed.** That is what makes it trustworthy without being read.

**And add undo inside that window.** A mis-tap forty times a morning is certain. The ledger is append-only so undo is a correcting entry, never a deletion — the original disposition stays visible, which is the point of the ledger.

---

## Q4 · Expected value — the formula, and it must not be invented

```
expected value  =  (unit gross + attached gross)  ×  stage probability
```

**Unit gross** — from the price master: ex-showroom less dealer cost, per variant. Where a dealer will not load cost, a per-model default set by the dealer admin.

**Attached gross** — exchange margin, finance payout, insurance commission and accessories, **each multiplied by its own attach rate for that model at that dealership.** Not the best case. The average case.

**Stage probability** — historical conversion from that stage to a delivered car, cut by source. Meta at Qualified converts differently from a walk-in at Qualified and the number should say so.

**Two rules, and the second matters more.**

**It is a ranking device before it is a reported figure.** Its job is to order the queue. Precision to the rupee is not required; being right about which call to make first is.

**It is computed from the dealer's own history, and at launch there is none.** So it starts from a seeded default probability table and is **replaced by the dealer's own numbers after the first month.** Same standing pattern as every other threshold on this programme: a number about behaviour is set from real behaviour. Until then the screen says the figure is provisional, because a confident number derived from nothing is worse than an honest one.

---

## Q5 · Duration is not a demonstration requirement. It is a points requirement.

**Not needed for the demonstration.** Attempt count, disposition and the recording being *available* carry it. Nobody watching a demonstration will ask how long the call was.

**But the points engine cannot ship without it.** The anti-gaming rule is that a connection under twenty seconds earns nothing — that is what stops dialling and hanging up from scoring. Without duration the rule cannot be enforced, and points without it are gameable on day one.

**So: defer telephony past the demonstration, and treat it as a hard dependency of Part 11.** Do not ship points and add duration afterwards. That order gets a floor into the habit of gaming a score before the control exists.

---

## Q6 · Phase 6, and do not fake it in the meantime

*"His wife has serviced a Swift here six times"* needs Household and Service. Neither exists. **It is Phase 6 and I would rather it arrive late and true than early and approximate.**

**But a weaker version is available now and worth having**, because one customer with many enquiries is live as of yesterday: *"This customer has two open enquiries with us"* or *"enquired about a Baleno in March."* Same shape, same purpose — the console reads as a briefing rather than a form — from data you already hold.

Build the slot now with the weak line in it. When Household and Service land, the strong line drops into the same place and no screen changes.

---

## Q7 · Parked is derived. Search is the phone number.

**Parked is not a stage and not a stored flag.** It is derived: **the latest disposition is *postponed* and its revisit date is in the future.** When that date arrives the lead is simply due, and it leaves Parked without anything being written. Same pattern as chain state and exception state — derived, never stored, so it cannot drift from the thing it describes.

That makes the chip honest rather than quietly meaning something else, which was the right instinct not to build it.

**Search: the phone number first, and it is not close.** Every inbound call, every walk-in, every duplicate check starts there. Partial matching from four digits. **Name second** — spelling is unreliable in three scripts. **Enquiry ID third**, and only because it appears on printed paperwork.

**Filters that map onto what you hold today:** Open, Overdue, Won, Lost, plus Model, Source and Stage. **Parked arrives with the postponement outcome.** Ship the six that work rather than five plus a chip that lies.

---

## Q8 · Yes. A seat names its workspace. Confirmed.

You are right that department carries no signal — telecalling is deliberately bound to sales because telecallers work the sales pipeline, so routing on department cannot work.

**A seat should carry a `workspace` field naming where that person lands.** Small structural addition, confirmed as a product decision, and it is the thing that makes the twenty-two-role menu real rather than decorative.

**Two rules with it.** A seat has exactly one landing workspace, never a list — a person who lands on a chooser has been given a decision instead of a day. And **workspace is separate from permission**: a branch manager lands on his decisions screen and can still reach telecalling. Landing is where you start; permission is what you may open.

---

## On section 06

Three failures, all found and disclosed by you: a repair miscounted from a scratch copy, a test that passed on the defect it named, and a delete aimed at scratch that connected to production.

**The third one is the serious one** and it deserves more than a line in a note — a command that reads its connection from a file and ignores the environment will do it again in a different script. It was stopped by a guard written last month for an unrelated reason, which is luck rather than design.

**But disclosing all three unprompted is why section 02's numbers are worth reading**, and that is exactly the right trade. A team that reports its own near-miss is a team whose figures I can build on.

---

*Nothing here needs a reply. Q1 to Q3 are hours each and land in the current two days. Q2 changes prototype copy and that is mine to do.*
```
